wifi.emptyBody: Tap Check WiFi now to measure the speed of the connection in use.
wifi.emptyHistory: No test history yet. Results from tests you have run will appear here.
wifi.fixLimitation: The web version cannot open the WiFi settings on your phone directly. The steps above need to be done yourself from your phone settings or the router page.
wifi.guideBaseline: As a guide, a reasonable download speed is usually around 1 MB/second or more. If the test result is far below that, something needs checking.
wifi.guideCommonCause: A common cause is a router setting that still uses an old mode. The old mode limits the speed of the whole WiFi network, even when the signal looks full.
wifi.guideTest1: Try another phone on the same WiFi. If the other phone is slow too, the problem is in the router or the network, not your phone.
wifi.guideTest2: Try mobile data. If mobile data is fine, the problem is in the WiFi, not your phone.
wifi.guideTitle: Slow WiFi: how to find the cause
wifi.latencyExplanation: HTTP latency is the time one small request takes to go to the server and back. The browser cannot measure a regular ping, so what is shown is HTTP latency.
wifi.manualDesc: The browser cannot read the WiFi name, signal strength, and channel directly. If you know them, for example from the router settings page, enter them here to make the result more complete. You may leave them blank.
wifi.notSavedNote: The result is not saved because you are not signed in. Sign in to save your history.
wifi.recChannel: If it is still slow, change the 2.4 GHz router channel to 1, 6, or 11. Those three channels do not interfere with each other.
wifi.recCloseDownloads: Close downloads or videos running on other devices, then test again.
wifi.recDns: Try changing the DNS to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 from the network settings on your phone.
wifi.recForgetNetwork: Try forgetting this WiFi network, then connect again by entering the password.
wifi.recNearRouter: Try moving closer to the router, then test again.
wifi.recRouterMode: Check the router mode on the router settings page. If it still uses an old mode, change it to mixed mode (b/g/n) so the speed is not limited.
wifi.savedNote: Tap Save report to save the result to your history.
wifi.shareText: Dokter HP WiFi test: download speed {{speed}} ({{classification}}), latency {{latency}}. Measured {{date}}, {{time}}.
wifi.speedFairDesc: Enough for everyday use, but not ideal for high-quality video.
wifi.speedFastDesc: Fast. Enough for video, calls, and everyday downloads.
wifi.speedSlowDesc: Slow. Messages and light pages still work, but video and downloads will stutter.
wifi.speedVeryFastDesc: Very fast. This connection is more than enough for everyday use.
wifi.speedVerySlowDesc: Very slow. Even opening a page will feel heavy. See the guide below to find the cause.
wifi.subtitle: Measure WiFi speed and find the cause when it is slow.
wifi.sustainedDesc: This test measures speed for a full 30 seconds to see whether the speed holds from start to finish, or starts fast and then drops halfway.
wifi.sustainedDropped: Speed started at {{start}} then dropped to {{end}}. A pattern like this usually comes from the router or the network, not the phone.
wifi.sustainedUnstable: Speed did not stay stable for 30 seconds. Try again when the network is not being used by other devices.
wifi.title: WiFi Doctor
